Just spent hours until I found this out. I couldn't upgrade to Windows 10 and always got the error 80240020. All the solutions you find online did not help. After I tried to start the setup.exe from a Windows 10 ISO I finally got a message that helps:"Could not update the system reserved partition".

Turns out that windows has a reserved partition. The Samsung Migration tool doesn't copy that one with the same size and it is too small. You need to use a 3rd party partition tool to change the size of the "*: Data"-partition on your SSD and resize it to ~350MB. After that I had to delete the content of the Download folder in c:\windows\SoftwareDistribution and force the download again, then use the FixIt Tool from Microsoft to fix the errors and then force the download one last time.

Hope that helps someone :)

In reading the article, this actually seems to be much more than your typical trite hit piece. They're definitely throwing GamerGate under the bus, but in the same process they're denouncing and specifically referencing the harassing tactics primarily used by socjus types. The gist of the article is that harassing people, even if you don't agree with them, is not necessarily a smart thing to do. If they have to use GamerGate as the sacrificial lamb to get a glimmer of self awareness into the skulls of some of these people then I have no complaints. Quoting the article:

We as a society deemed campaigns such as Gamergate unacceptable and rejected their proponents as harassers who crossed the line. But because we all agree that we dislike Palmer, the campaign against him has so far been deemed acceptable, even funny or laudable.

That worries me. And it should worry you. Gamergate has been run out of polite internet society, but the mob campaign against Palmer suggests that the tactics Gamergate employed are not disappearing — they are becoming more mainstream. That should be deeply worrying to us all.

What Palmer did was wrong, and he deserves to be punished to the full extent of the law. But it's easy to forget just how dangerous and unjust "mob justice" is while it's targeting someone you despise. The more this behavior is normalized, the more likely it is to be deployed against targets who might not necessarily deserve to have their lives destroyed — including, perhaps one day, against you.
